title: Prune the slopvac compile cache
description:
~/.cache/slopvac/ accumulates one directory per ruleset fingerprint and never removes any. Observed: 209 directories, 83M, on a single development machine. Each ruleset edit, severity change, profile change, or blocklist edit mints a new key, so the growth is proportional to development activity rather than to use.

No correctness impact -- the fingerprint check means a stale entry is never served -- but it is unbounded disk growth in a user cache directory.

Options: prune by mtime on compile (keep the N most recent), or a 'slopvac cache prune' subcommand, or both.
close_reason: Both options implemented in 90d177f: LRU prune to CACHE_KEEP=16 on every compile that owns the shared cache (mtime refreshed on cache hit, so use beats recency of build), plus a 'slopvac cache' subcommand with --prune and --all. 209 trees/83M -> 16/1.0MiB. Documented in README.

title: Evaluate Vale script checks (Tengo) for genre structure rules
description:
Vale's `extends: script` check runs a Tengo script over the document and can
assert on structure, not just on token patterns. Verified with vale 3.15.2 during
the 2026-07-27 style audit: a script check reporting "consumer doc has no
'## Install' heading" fires at 1:1 on a document that lacks it.

Every rule slopvac ships is a regex over prose. That reaches wording and misses
shape, so the gate cannot tell a README with no install section from one that has
three, or catch an ADR with a Decision heading and no Consequences. The
`write-docs` skill states its genre rules in prose and nothing enforces them.

## What a script check can reach

- required headings per genre (consumer: Install, Usage; ADR: Context, Decision,
  Consequences; CONTRIBUTING: how to run the tests)
- heading order and nesting depth
- a fenced code block with no language tag
- a link with no target
- a table whose header count and row cell counts disagree
- section length ratios: a section padded to match a sibling

## Why this is not done yet

The mechanism is the easy half. The hard half is deciding what each genre MUST
contain, and that is a house position rather than a measurement. Getting it wrong
produces a rule that fires on every document a project already has, which is how
a gate gets switched off.

Blocked on that decision, not on the mechanism.
design:
A new style, `prose-genre`, one rule per structural assertion, all at warning.

Mechanism, verified with vale 3.15.2:

    extends: script
    message: "%s"
    level: warning
    scope: raw
    script: |
      text := import("text")
      matches := []
      if !text.contains(scope, "## Install") {
        matches = append(matches, {begin: 0, end: 1,
          message: "consumer doc has no '## Install' heading"})
      }

`scope: raw` hands the script the whole document. The `matches` array is what
Vale reports, and each entry needs `begin`, `end`, and `message`. Reporting at
0:1 anchors the finding to the top of the file, which is right for a
whole-document assertion: there is no line to point at when the defect is an
absence.

Routing follows the genre sections already in `vale.ini.template`. A required
heading for a consumer README is wrong for a commit message, so each rule is
scoped to the genre it belongs to rather than switched off everywhere else.

Open questions to settle before writing rules:

- Which headings are genuinely required per genre, and which are conventions this
  project happens to like? Anything in the second group does not ship.
- Does the assertion belong in Vale at all, or in the `review-docs` judgement
  pass? Vale gives determinism and a file:line; the skill gives reasons. A
  missing Install section is mechanical, so Vale. "The heading promises something
  the section withholds" is not, so the skill.
- Tengo has no filesystem access, so a relative-link check cannot verify the path
  exists. That one needs a script outside Vale.
acceptance_criteria:
A decision recorded either way.

If adopted: a prose-genre style with per-genre structural rules, each with a
fixture proving it fires on an absence and stays quiet on a conforming document,
routed through the existing genre sections in vale.ini.template, and picked up by
gen-rule-table.py.

If rejected: the reason written down so the next style audit does not re-derive
the mechanism from scratch.
close_reason: Embedding rejected with an explicit architecture decision; no missing rule justifies a second runtime.
